output.brief: The Android drop is almost certainly caused by a new vendor rule, not by release 6.14. Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks password logins from the app's networking library when no edge session cookie is present. Blocking began at 10:41 UTC, a minute or so after the pack went live. The failures are HTTP 403s on password submissions only, on every app version, OS version and patch level. Version 6.14 is only 5% of attempts and fails at the same rate as older versions, so a rollback would not help. The blocked requests come from about 41,300 real installs, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before. iOS, web and quick-unlock are unaffected. That does not look like bot traffic. Next step: ask Corvane to put that rule into log-only mode on the mobile password path, keeping all other protections, then check that password-login success recovers. Don't raise bot sensitivity or drop blocked attempts from the KPI. Both would hide or worsen the problem. Continue the 6.14 rollout. I'm fairly confident (about 90%). Ask Corvane for the rule logic and a fix for the missing cookie condition.
